Hi Léonard,

Thanks again for taking my (slightly noisy) cold call this afternoon,
appreciated you walking me through how Overstory actually works under the
hood. Quick recap, plus everything you need to filter whether Encord is
worth a conversation with the ML team.

What I took away from our chat:

   - Overstory produces vegetation encroachment maps for electric
   distribution and transmission utilities so they can prioritise cuts and the
   highest-risk corridors.
   - The pipeline today combines manual pole annotation, co-registration
   (stretching imagery, keeping registration points to use downstream), and a
   hybrid AI + human pass for declining trees, with specialist arborists
   validating sick trees across entire forests.
   - You're the right person to filter whether Encord is interesting; the
   ML pipeline tooling decisions sit elsewhere on the team.

Why I think Encord is worth a serious look for Overstory:

Encord is the data layer that sits between your imagery and your models:
annotation, curation, model evaluation, and active-learning loops in one
place. The pieces I think map most directly to what you described:

   - Geospatial-native labeling: large satellite tiles, multi-spectral /
   multi-modal, polygon and segmentation tooling for tree crowns, conductors,
   poles and right-of-way. SAM 3 integration meaningfully cuts the manual
   segmentation burden.
   - Hybrid AI + expert review workflows: consensus scoring and reviewer
   routing for the arborist validation step.
   - Active learning and data curation (Index + Active): surface the
   imagery patches and edge cases that move model performance most: useful
   when you're trying to scale fuel detection without scaling labeling cost
   linearly.
   - Model evaluation: regression-test models against labeled ground truth
   as you push new versions, with slice-level performance on rare species,
   occlusion, seasonality, etc.
